# Helmlab

> Helmlab is a perceptual color space library shipping two purpose-built Lab spaces: GenSpace for color generation (palettes, gradients, gamut mapping) and MetricSpace for color difference measurement. GenSpace beats OKLab 66-9 across 90 benchmarks; MetricSpace v21 achieves STRESS 22.48 on COMBVD, beating CIEDE2000 by 23%. Available as MIT-licensed Python and JavaScript packages with zero dependencies.

Helmlab solves three problems that existing color spaces fail at: blue-to-white gradients shifting toward lavender (OKLab), uneven lightness scales causing "dark holes" in palettes at 700-800, and inaccurate perceptual distance prediction. The library is the first to achieve state-of-the-art in both visual generation quality and perceptual color difference simultaneously.

Important notes:
- Helmlab is a JavaScript/Python library that outputs standard hex/RGB values. It is NOT a CSS color function — use `oklch()` for native CSS interpolation.
- MetricSpace's published STRESS 22.48 is a training metric. Cross-validated estimate is ~24.3 (still #1 among all competitors including CIEDE2000 at 29.20).
- GenSpace loses 9 of 90 benchmarks to OKLab — notably near-achromatic gradients (24% gap) and CVD deutan distinguishability (43% gap).

## Docs

- [Documentation](https://helmlab.space/docs): Full API reference for Python and JavaScript with identical method signatures
- [Quick Start](https://helmlab.space/docs#quick-start): Three-line install and usage example
- [GenSpace API](https://helmlab.space/docs#genspace): Forward/inverse transforms, gradient, palette, semanticScale methods
- [MetricSpace API](https://helmlab.space/docs#metricspace): deltaE, perceptualDistance, contrastRatio, ensureContrast methods
- [TypeScript types](https://helmlab.space/docs#typescript): Type definitions for GenParams, MetricParams, and Helmlab class

## Benchmarks

- [Full benchmark report](https://helmlab.space/benchmark): 90 metrics across 13 categories, complete transparency including losses
- [STRESS scores](https://helmlab.space/benchmark#stress): Comparison vs 9 competitors (CIEDE2000, CIE94, DIN99, OKLab, Jzazbz, CAM16-UCS, etc.) on 3 psychophysical datasets
- [Independent validation](https://helmlab.space/benchmark#independent): Hung-Berns 1995, Ebner-Fairchild 1998, Pointer 1980 — datasets OKLab was optimized on, where GenSpace wins 6-1
- [Overfitting analysis](https://helmlab.space/benchmark#overfitting): Train/test split results showing +1.8 STRESS gap, still beats all competitors

## Tools

- [Interactive playground](https://helmlab.space/playground): Live tools running helmlab.js client-side
- [Gradient Tool](https://helmlab.space/playground#gradient): Helmlab vs OKLab vs CIE Lab side-by-side with CV uniformity badges
- [Palette Generator](https://helmlab.space/playground#palette): 50-950 Tailwind-style scales from any base color
- [Distance Calculator](https://helmlab.space/playground#distance): MetricSpace deltaE with JND interpretation
- [Contrast Checker](https://helmlab.space/playground#contrast): WCAG checker with hue-preserving auto-fix
- [Color Harmony](https://helmlab.space/playground#harmony): Complementary, analogous, triadic, tetradic, split-complementary
- [Mode Adapter](https://helmlab.space/playground#mode): Light/dark mode color adaptation with contrast verification

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/Grkmyldz148/helmlab): MIT-licensed source code, ColorBench benchmarks, optimization scripts
- [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/helmlab): JavaScript/TypeScript package, 11.6 KB gzipped, zero dependencies
- [PyPI package](https://pypi.org/project/helmlab/): Python package
- [Research paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.23010): Academic paper on the perceptual color space methodology

## Optional

- [BENCHMARK.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Grkmyldz148/helmlab/main/BENCHMARK.md): Full 560-line benchmark report with all 90 metric values, sub-dataset breakdowns, and architecture diagrams
- [GenSpace pipeline details](https://helmlab.space/benchmark#genspace-architecture): XYZ to M1 to depcubic transfer to M2 to enrichment to neutral correction
- [MetricSpace pipeline details](https://helmlab.space/benchmark#metricspace-architecture): 13-stage enriched pipeline with Bradford CAT, Helmholtz-Kohlrausch correction, and pair-dependent SL/SC weighting
- [color.js integration PR](https://github.com/color-js/color.js/pull/722): Pull request adding Helmlab to color.js
